audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers read Jax, Skill, Skill, Skill, Skill, Skill, Jax. The packet chart is Volibear, Skill, Jax, Jax, Jax, Jax, Jax, the win rate is 58.23%, and the page's own whys say Jax concedes level 1 (whys[0]: 'farm safely and concede the opener') and owns everything from 3 onward.
audit.why: Frenzied Maul on a flat 5s cooldown with its recast heal out-sustains Jax before Counter Strike exists, so level 1 is Volibear's. From 3 Counter Strike dodges the auto string his entire all-in is built from, and nothing in his kit reverses that later.
audit.corrected: Chart set to Volibear, Skill, Jax, Jax, Jax, Jax, Jax across both layers as one atomic group, ratings adjusted to match.

audit.whatIsWrong: Jax's ultimate is called "Grandmaster at Arms" in whys[4], spikes[2].text and mid; Volibear's passive is written "Relentless Storm" in whys[0], spikes[1].text and early.
audit.why: The abilities are Grandmaster's Might (110/100/90s) and The Relentless Storm. phases[4].why on the same page already uses Grandmaster's Might, so the page contradicts itself; the packet's near-miss detector flagged the passive at distance 4.
audit.corrected: Both names corrected everywhere they appear in prose. Jax's own passive is already correctly named Relentless Assault and was left alone.

audit.whatIsWrong: Thundering Smash is called 'his engage' with no cooldown, so 'bait it' has no timer. wants.foe[0] also contains a Cyrillic character in "CС'd".
audit.why: Thundering Smash is 12s at rank 1 and only drops to 10s at rank 5, while Counter Strike is 17s at rank 1 — Jax's answer is on a longer cooldown than the threat, which is exactly why baiting matters and why the number belongs on the page. Sky Splitter is a flat 16s and Stormbringer 160s at rank 1.
audit.corrected: dosFull[0].d now names the 12s cooldown; the Cyrillic character in wants.foe[0] replaced with ASCII. The existing note that Counter Strike's dodge does not stop Sky Splitter or the Q-stun itself is correct and was kept.

audit.why: The warning that Stormbringer disables your tower — so you reset rather than trade into a dive — is in the kit text and already on the page.

edits.before: Volibear's level 1-2 is genuinely scary - his W (Frenzied Maul) wounds you and the recast heals him off your missing HP, and Relentless Storm stacks attack speed so his autos chunk you while he sustains, and you have no Counter Strike yet to punish it, so don't trade, just farm safely. The lane flips the instant you hit 3: hold E, let him commit the Q run-down into W-bite autos, dodge the whole auto string, then recast to stun and drop Leap Strike + Empower on him. The one thing that wrecks you early is eating his Q (Thundering Smash) stun from fog - never facecheck, because a run-down stun into his full bite combo is the only way he kills you before items.
edits.after: Volibear's level 1-2 is genuinely scary - his W (Frenzied Maul) is a flat 5s cooldown, so he wounds you and recasts to heal off your missing HP faster than you can answer, and The Relentless Storm stacks attack speed so his autos chunk you while he sustains. With no Counter Strike yet, don't trade, just farm. The lane flips the instant you hit 3: hold E, let him commit the Q run-down into W-bite autos, dodge the whole auto string, then recast to stun and drop Leap Strike + Empower on him. What wrecks you early is eating his Q (Thundering Smash, 12s) stun from fog - never facecheck, because that run-down into his full bite combo is the only way he kills you before items.

edits.before: This is where you take over, and the reason is mechanical: Voli's all-in leans on auto attacks - he runs you down with Q, bites with W, and his stacked Relentless Storm autos do the work - and Counter Strike dodges exactly that, so bait the engage, E through the auto string, stun, and out-trade him before his W recast-heal can top him back up. Just know the E-dodge does NOT stop his Sky Splitter (E) lightning nuke or the Q-stun auto itself, so time the recast for the autos, not the spells. At 6 you spike past him: Grandmaster at Arms' instant Armor/MR steroid eats his burst and the on-hit ramp grinds him down in the extended brawl he wants. Respect that his R disables your tower, so back off and reset rather than feed a dive when you're low.
